data.name: Tejshvara
data.gender_notes: Tejshvara is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who has control over energy and power, a wise and powerful leader. The name Tejshvara carries the meaning “Lord of Energy and Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Tejshvara usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of energy and power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who seek to harness the power of the divine and use it for the greater good.
data.etymology: Tejshvara belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Energy and Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tejshvara total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tejshvara holds great significance in Hindu mythology and culture. Tej means "might, power, and energy," while Shvara denotes "lord or master." Together, the name signifies one who possesses supreme power, wisdom, and control over the energy around them. In Hindu folklore, Tejshvara is a revered name for leaders, heroes, and spiritual guides, evoking a sense of strength, courage, and authority.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Tejshvara represents the divine energy and power that lies within every individual. It signifies the connection between the innate inner power and the universe. The name serves as a reminder for individuals to tap into their inner strength and wisdom to navigate life's challenges and strive towards personal growth. As such, Tejshvara carries a deep spiritual meaning, inspiring a sense of self-awareness,右shift self-mastery, and a deep reverence for the power of the inner self.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tejshvara: One who has mastery over Tejas, or divine energy and radiance, symbolizing inner strength, willpower, and illumination. Spiritually, it represents the ability to harness and channel this energy for personal growth and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Tejshvara is a name of Lord Indra, the king of gods in Hindu mythology. He is the god of rain, thunderbolts, and the sky. He is also known as the god of victory and is often depicted carrying a thunderbolt or a bow and arrow.

historical_references.reference: Tejshvara was a Chalukya king who ruled from 1127 to 1132 CE in the Vengi kingdom of the Deccan plateau in India. He succeeded his father Vijayaditya and was succeeded by his son Bijjala II.
historical_references.context: Chalukya Dynasty, Vengi Kingdom, Deccan Plateau, India

historical_references.reference: Tejashwara or Tejashankara was a Jain monk and scholar who lived around the 12th century CE. He was a disciple of Hemachandra and played a significant role in the development of the Digambara Monastic traditions in India.
historical_references.context: Jain Monastic Traditions, Digambara Sect, India
